verdict: PayPal moved $486B of payments (+10%) and grew revenue 5% to $8.7B, but profit fell 12% to $1.1B as costs rose faster than revenue — management still raised full-year non-GAAP guidance on the transformation plan.

segments.name: Transaction revenues
segments.note: The cut PayPal takes on every payment it processes — $486B of payment volume flowed through in the quarter, up 10%, across 6.8 billion transactions.

segments.name: Revenues from other value added services
segments.note: Interest on customer balances, partner fees and other services around the core payment.

flow.costPlain: What each payment costs PayPal to run: $4,385M of transaction expense (card-network and processing fees) plus $397M of transaction and credit losses on its loans.

opex.name: Customer support and operations
opex.note: Support staff and the cost of running payment operations.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Marketing, and winning merchants and users.

opex.name: Technology and development
opex.note: Building and running the PayPal and Venmo platforms.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company: finance, legal, risk and offices.

opex.name: Restructuring and other
opex.note: Severance and reshaping costs as PayPal works through its transformation plan.

takeaways.title: The pipes keep growing
takeaways.text: Total payment volume rose 10% to $486.4B and transactions rose 8% to 6.8 billion, with 439 million active accounts. Venmo and Braintree kept their momentum, and branded checkout stabilized.

takeaways.title: What PayPal keeps barely grew
takeaways.text: Transaction margin dollars rose just 1% to $3.9B (3% excluding interest on customer balances). Revenue grew 5%, but transaction costs grew faster — the margin squeeze is the story of the turnaround.

takeaways.title: Buybacks and a guidance raise
takeaways.text: PayPal returned $1.5B to shareholders via buybacks in the quarter ($6.0B over twelve months), paid a $0.14 dividend, and raised full-year non-GAAP guidance while reaffirming GAAP EPS guidance.

oneTimers: GAAP EPS includes a roughly $0.07 negative impact from PayPal's strategic investment portfolio and crypto assets held for investment, versus a $0.01 positive impact a year ago — that swing sits inside the $117M of other expense.
Restructuring and other charges were $113M in the quarter as the transformation plan reshapes the company.
otherDetail: Other income (expense), net was −$117M, including losses on PayPal's strategic investment portfolio and crypto assets held for investment.
follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference.
